Thanks for the context and the sample. Quick recommendation below — high level so Sofia can share with Finex. I attached a rough estimate workbook (redwood-dedicated-estimate-v1.xlsx) and a VPC checklist (vpc-checklist.pdf).

Summary assumptions (from the sample):
- Avg token per chat request: ~800 tokens (prompt + completion).
- Sustained chat: 45 TPS -> ~36k tokens/sec. Peak burst: 320 TPS -> ~256k tokens/sec (short windows).
- Batch jobs: large token volume but scheduled — we route to a separate worker queue in Dedicated pool.

Option A — Latency-first (recommended for initial PoC if p95/p99 are critical):
- GPU mix: 4 x NVIDIA H100-80GB (quantized FP16 or 4-bit where we can keep quality).
- Per-GPU expected sustained throughput (chat-like, with our runtime and batching): ~70 TPS (with 16 concurrent worker slots, small batch target to keep latency low).
- Pool sizing: initial reserved pool of 4 H100s gives ~280 TPS sustained capacity; handles sustained + short bursts when combined with autoscale/burst credit.
- Latency: expected p95 ~350–420ms, p99 ~600–750ms depending on network/VPC tail; meets Finex target in most scenarios.

Option B — Cost-first (trade latency for lower infra cost):
- GPU mix: 6 x A100-40GB (cheaper per-hour, slightly lower single-request latency but higher batching efficiency).
- Per-GPU expected sustained throughput: ~45 TPS (with 24 concurrent worker slots, larger batch sizes during non-peak).
- Pool sizing: 6 A100s ~270 TPS sustained. For short bursts, recommend a small burst pool (2 H100s on-demand) or fall back to Hosted on overflow.
- Latency: p95 ~480–650ms, p99 ~850ms (may occasionally miss p99 target under network tail).

Operational notes and tuning:
- KV/prefix caching: strongly recommend enabling prefix caching for chat flows to reduce tokens/sec in hot sessions. This will reduce per-GPU load by ~10–20% for session-heavy customers.
- Quantization: 4-bit quantization for both options gives dramatic cost savings; for latency-first keep FP16 fallback for critical endpoints. We should include an A/B eval during PoC.
- Autoscale/burst policy: configure 2–3x burst credit for 3–5 minute windows. For Finex's 320 TPS spikes, both mixes handle bursts with recommended burst pool.
- Network/VPC: Finex asked for customer-managed peering — provide the vpc-checklist.pdf and a one-page network diagram for procurement.

Rough cost delta vs Hosted (very rough estimate):
- Option A (4xH100 reserved): ~1.8–2.3x the Hosted bill for the same sustained tokens (higher baseline infra but better tail latency).
- Option B (6xA100 reserved + occasional Hosted overflow): ~1.2–1.6x Hosted.

Next steps:

2) If they pick latency-first, we send a 3-week PoC plan + PoC SOW and schedule security questionnaire handoff to Security/Compliance.
3) If they need exact pricing, Ben to prepare a formal PO/quote using the attached workbook.

Ben — tagging you for pricing worksheet and any procurement notes.
